sections.content: How many people are "human resources administrative occupations"?

23,910 people

were counted on the census as "human resources administrative occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Human resources administrative occupations provide administrative support for the human resources (HR) operations within organisations.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "human resources administrative occupations" there were more women than men (85.6% compared with 14.4%).

This means "human resources administrative occupations" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 14.3% and women made up 85.7% of "human resources administrative occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "human resources administrative occupations" included:

  • complementary health associate professionals
  • special and additional needs education teaching professionals
  • health care practice managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "human resources administrative occupations", 15.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "human resources administrative occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "human resources administrative occupations" included:

  • data entry administrators
  • vehicle and parts salespersons and advisers
  • pensions and insurance clerks and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "human resources administrative occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "human resources administrative occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "human resources administrative occupations", 10.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (66.8% compared with 33.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.9%) than self-employed (2.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
